subtopics.title: Two Accounts, One Total — Defining Mechanical Energy

questions.question: Mechanical energy is defined as:
options: The energy an object has because of its temperature
The sum of an object's gravitational potential energy and kinetic energy
The difference between potential and kinetic energy
The energy stored in a stretched spring only

questions.question: A 4 kg ball rests on a roof 15 m above the ground (reference at the ground). Its mechanical energy is:
Energy quantities such as E p and E k are:
options: Scalars measured in joules — size only, no direction

subtopics.title: The Law of Conservation and Its Mechanical Special Case

questions.question: The law of conservation of energy states that energy:
options: Slowly runs out as objects move
Is created by gravity and destroyed by friction
Can be destroyed but never created
Cannot be created or destroyed — only transferred or converted

questions.question: Mechanical energy is conserved only when:
options: No friction or air resistance acts on the object
The object moves in a straight line
The object is heavier than 1 kilogram

questions.question: During a frictionless fall, the principle of conservation of mechanical energy claims that:
options: The sum of kinetic and potential energy stays constant

questions.question: A block slides across a rough floor and stops. The correct energy statement is:
options: Total energy was destroyed by the roughness
Mechanical energy decreased — it transferred to heat — while total energy stayed conserved
Kinetic energy converted entirely to potential energy

subtopics.title: The Falling Ball — Working the Energy Ledger

questions.question: The 4 kg ball falls from 15 m. At 7,5 m its kinetic energy is:
At the halfway mark, the ball's speed is found from ½ × 4 × v² = 294, giving:
The instant before the ground, the ball's energy account reads:
options: E p = 588 J and E k = 0
E p = 294 J and E k = 294 J
E p = 0 and E k = 294 J
E p = 0 and E k = 588 J

questions.question: Setting ½mv² = mgh and cancelling the mass shows that landing speed:
options: Depends only on the drop height, through v² = 2gh
Cannot be found without the time of fall

subtopics.title: Reference Points, Leaks and the Habits That Bank the Marks

questions.question: The reference point in an energy problem is:
options: Always the top of the fall
Your chosen level where h = 0, held fixed for the whole problem
Different for each position you calculate

questions.question: Using g = 10 instead of 9,8 for the rooftop ball turns 588 J into:
The kinetic energy of the ball moving at 12,12 m/s is ½ × 4 × 12,12², which equals about:
Which phrase in a question licenses the equation E k1 + E p1 = E k2 + E p2?
In the wallet picture, the height pocket and speed pocket hold, respectively:
The wallet is sealed — no money enters or leaves — as long as:
options: The object is lighter than 10 kg
Nothing rubs: no friction and no air resistance
The floor is chosen at the ground

questions.question: Choosing where height counts as zero is:
options: Your decision — any level works, but it must hold for the whole problem
Fixed by the equation as the ground

questions.question: The rooftop ball's three wallet snapshots, top to bottom, read:
The energy method found the landing speed without using:
options: Timing, acceleration or equations of motion

questions.question: If your two pockets stop adding up to the sealed total, it means:
options: The principle of conservation has failed
An arithmetic slip is hiding in your working
The ball has gained energy from the air
The reference point moved by itself

questions.question: A 40 kg toolbox and a 4 kg ball leave the same 15 m roof (no air resistance). Their landing speeds are:
options: The toolbox lands ten times faster
The ball lands ten times faster
Impossible to compare without the time

questions.question: Mass cancels from the landing-speed calculation because heavier objects:
options: Carry more energy AND need proportionally more energy for the same speed

questions.question: When friction leaks energy out of the mechanical wallet, the leaked joules:
options: Return to the height pocket later
Leave as heat and sound — still existing, but outside both pockets

questions.question: The warm rim of a bicycle brake after a long stop is direct evidence of:
options: Kinetic energy converted to heat by friction
Potential energy stored in the metal
